title: Multi Source Flood Fill
summary: Given a grid size n by m, and an initial coloring of some cells, each cell spreads its color to adjacent uncolored cells simultaneously.
statement: Given a grid size n by m, and an initial coloring of some cells, each cell spreads its color to adjacent uncolored cells simultaneously. If multiple colors reach the same cell, it takes the color with the highest value. The process repeats until no more cells can be colored, then return the final grid state.
constraints: n and m are positive; sources contains distinct in-bounds [row,column,color] entries with positive colors.
Every round, colored cells spread to orthogonal uncolored neighbors simultaneously.
When colors arrive in the same earliest round, use the greatest color; return the filled grid.
hints: Arrival time is Manhattan-distance BFS from all sources.
Process one complete frontier per round and collect candidates for still-uncolored neighbors.
Resolve all same-round candidates by maximum color before writing any cell.
Level batching guarantees earliest arrival; delayed writes preserve simultaneity and the maximum rule.
editorial: Level batching guarantees earliest arrival; delayed writes preserve simultaneity and the maximum rule.

tests.explanation: Distance ties favor color two, producing [[1,1,2],[1,2,2],[2,2,2]].
The sole color spreads right each round, filling [1,1,1].
